netconf.transport: persistent simulated TCP, logical SSH authentication; no cryptography
netconf.authentication: privilege 15 local or shared AAA with actual delivered RADIUS
constraints: Only default merge; supported per-interface operations; invalid clone changes never commit
Shared candidate and session-owned locks; simultaneous CLI conflict rejects commit
Confirmed commit default 600 seconds, explicit 1–65535; actual virtual timeout/session-loss rollback
Idle session expires after 120 seconds of virtual time; reset/disable/mode change clears channels/locks
Conditional advertised capabilities correspond to implemented RPCs
netconf.monitoring: show netconf-yang sessions [detail|session-id], datastores and operational summary read real sessionSnapshot/state; MGMT-MON-01

restconf.transport: simulated HTTPS/TCP; logical TLS, no cryptography
restconf.authentication: privilege 15 local or configured shared AAA; HTTP access-class before datastore handler

resources.behavior: Supported operational interfaces and native hostname
Read or atomically update actual IOS hostname
Read, transactionally merge entries or create virtual interfaces; collection PUT rejects
RFC7951 list-array entry, replacement/merge, or virtual interface deletion; physical deletion rejects
Actual leaf update/default reset; DELETE does not delete the interface

restconf.encoding: application/yang-data+json; RFC7951 list arrays; no-cache; structured errors
restconf.transaction: validate cloned DeviceConfig, enforce running locks/candidate conflict, atomically apply shared config

behavioralChain: Normal routed or switched TCP and interface ACLs
NETCONF RPC or RESTCONF structured resource validation
CLI show output, topology serialization and startup reload

testCases.title: MGMT-MON-01 show netconf-yang reports delivered authenticated sessions and actual candidate lock ownership
MD-01 RESTCONF GET uses authenticated delivered HTTPS and reports real interface/counter state
MD-02 RESTCONF interface edits affect routed traffic and invalid multi-edit transactions roll back
MD-03 RESTCONF native hostname and virtual interface changes share CLI, save/load and reload state
MD-04 normal inbound ACL and HTTP access-class enforce RESTCONF reachability independently of credentials
MD-05 NETCONF authenticates over a persistent TCP830 session and reads real XML configuration
MD-06 candidate is gated, isolated, shared and locked; commit applies, discard and session close release state
MD-07 confirmed commit times out through simulation clock and restores actual forwarding; confirmation persists
MD-08 session failure rolls back unconfirmed commit and power/reset clears locks, candidate and callbacks
MD-09 invalid XML/unknown model/partial edits never mutate running state; NETCONF disable terminates sessions
MD-10 NETCONF and RESTCONF AAA accounts authenticate through the real RADIUS server and preserve privilege requirements
MD-11 strict RESTCONF list/leaf encoding rejects ignored fields and deletion of a leaf preserves its interface
MD-12 candidate mode changes terminate sessions, NETCONF ACLs block delivery, and stale candidate edits never overwrite CLI changes
MD-13 NETCONF idle session expiry uses virtual time and releases candidate locks
MD-14 all five IOS XE teaching node profiles expose authenticated NETCONF and RESTCONF endpoints from actual interfaces
MD-15 NETCONF namespace/duplicate field validation and prototype-like interface keys reject without side effects
MD-16 lightweight AP does not advertise or accept unavailable model-driven service commands
MD-17 inherited entity and undeclared namespace names remain invalid XML without changing the datastore

verification.referenceComparison: documented primary Cisco/RFC invariants; no real Cisco exact-output/runtime golden

limitations: Logical SSH/TLS only; no external binary client interoperability
No general YANG schema/compiler/library or arbitrary Cisco models
IPv6 edits, notifications/subscriptions, XPath, NETCONF base1.1 absent
No NACM/model authorization, ETag/query options or YANG-patch
XML subtree retrieval is a selected native/interface subset, not arbitrary subtree projection
Full platform defaults, AAA policy and Cisco output equivalence remain unverified
